extraction.name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
extraction.description: A comprehensive benchmark for evaluating AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing. It contains 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories, including natural sounds, music, spoken dialogue, role-play imitation, multi-turn dialogue, and heterogeneous images.
extraction.creator: Ke Wang; Houxing Ren; Zimu Lu; Mingjie Zhan; Hongsheng Li
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was constructed by collecting source data from multiple existing datasets across listening, speaking, and viewing subsets, converting collected text instructions into audio, and then applying a four-stage curation process consisting of deduplication, validation, categorization, and sampling.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Incomplete or unsuitable instances were excluded during validation, including corrupted images and silent audio.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw/source data consisted of existing audio, text, and image datasets: audio clips with sounds, music, and speech; spoken-interaction tasks from text and audio datasets; and images from MMMU used with audio tasks.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human evaluation validation was conducted by randomly sampling 10% of Qwen2.5-Omni-7B's responses from each of 13 tasks (1050 examples), which were independently evaluated by human judges.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper analyzes annotation quality by comparing automated evaluation with human judgments using Pearson correlation coefficients and agreement rates; correlations range from 0.73 to 1.00 with an overall correlation of 0.92, and the overall agreement rate is 96.1%.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Automated evaluation/annotation used gpt-oss-20b to assess response texts, emotion2vec to derive emotion probabilities for prompts, Whisper-Large-v3 to transcribe speech outputs, UTMOS to score speech quality, and Wespeaker to calculate speaker similarity for role-play.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark may inherit biases from source data and design choices; academic or synthetic sources may not reflect real-world fairness concerns, and the fixed set of 100 role-play roles may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas. Automated and GPT-based evaluation may also introduce bias.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include limited diversity and mostly English-only content (aside from five Chinese roles), restricted model coverage, possible noise/bias from automated and GPT-based scoring, incomplete task realism and coverage (e.g., no video-audio integration or continuous streaming), and offline static evaluation that does not capture latency, partial utterances, barge-in, or error recovery. The dataset is also not intended for training models for cheating.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper discusses both beneficial and harmful social implications: the benchmark can support development of better voice assistants, but role-play voice imitation creates risks such as identity spoofing, harassment, fraud, impersonation, privacy violations, and unequal performance across demographics. The authors propose safeguards to minimize these harms.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Speaker identity/voice characteristics are included through role-play voice imitation and speaker similarity evaluation; the paper also mentions demographic considerations and includes language-related variation (English prompts and five Chinese roles).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Intended for evaluating voice assistants and reproducing benchmark results; meant for researchers to assess listening, speaking, and viewing capabilities. It is explicitly not intended for training models for cheating, and downstream voice imitation use should follow consent gating, watermarking/traceability, and safety-card guidance.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and code will be publicly released under an MIT license. The authors will maintain a data governance process for auditing and removal and reserve the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data were sampled to balance task ratios after categorization.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Texts were preprocessed for speech synthesis by replacing image-reference tokens with descriptive phrases, rewriting text for TTS readability and accurate pronunciation of numbers/math, rephrasing multiple-choice options, and curating data through deduplication and validation that removed duplicates and incomplete/unsuitable instances.

name.evidence: We introduce VoiceAssistant-Eval, a comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing.

description.evidence: We introduce VoiceAssistant-Eval, a comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing. VoiceAssistant-Eval comprises 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories.

creator.evidence: Ke Wang1,∗ Houxing Ren1,∗ Zimu Lu1 Mingjie Zhan2,† Hongsheng Li1,3,†

rai:dataCollection.evidence: “We collect source data from 23 audio understanding datasets... The collected text instructions are then converted into audio.” and “We improve data quality through a four-stage curation process: (1) Deduplication... (2) Validation... (3) Categorization... (4) Sampling...”

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: “We collect source data from 23 audio understanding datasets...” and “Other source data are from 22 datasets...” and “we select MMMU (Yue et al., 2024) as the source dataset.”

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: “Validation: We exclude incomplete or unsuitable instances, including entries with corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, and demonstrably incorrect answers.”

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: “This subset contains audio clips featuring a variety of sounds, music, human speech...” ; “Other source data are from 22 datasets, including 11 text datasets... and 11 audio datasets...” ; “This subset contains a wide variety of images from different domains... we select MMMU... as the source dataset.”

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: “We randomly sampled 10% of the model’s responses from each of the 13 tasks, resulting in 1050 examples. These responses are then independently evaluated by human judges.”

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: “All reported Pearson correlation coefficients between the model’s scores and human ratings are notably high (ranging from 0.73 to 1.00, with an overall correlation of 0.92)” and “The overall agreement rate is 96.1%.”

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: “For content quality, we use gpt-oss-20b ... to assess response texts” ; “for emotion, we use emotion2vec ...” ; “we first transcribe the speech outputs using Whisper-Large-v3” ; “To measure speech quality, we employ UTMOS” ; “we use Wespeaker ... to calculate the speaker similarity”

rai:dataBiases.evidence: VoiceAssistant-Eval may carry biases from its source data and design choices... The questions and contexts are drawn from academic or synthetic sources... For example, the role-play subset uses a fixed set of 100 roles and associated style prompts. These roles may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: all other prompts and evaluations are in English. This monolingual focus may not capture the full variability of real user interactions... We rely on automated measures and GPT-based scoring, which, while efficient, may introduce noise and bias... video-audio integration and continuous audio-visual streaming tasks are beyond the scope of this benchmark... evaluates models in an offline, static manner... The VoiceAssistant-Eval dataset is not supposed to be used, though the risk exists, for training models for cheating.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: To mitigate misuse risks (e.g., identity spoofing, harassment, fraud)... These measures aim to enable research on personalization while minimizing harms related to impersonation, privacy violations, and unequal performance across demographics.

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: because the benchmark includes role-play voice imitation and speaker similarity evaluation... minimizing harms related to impersonation, privacy violations, and unequal performance across demographics... Although we include five Chinese roles in the role-play task, all other prompts and evaluations are in English.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We intend for researchers to use this dataset to better evaluate voice assistants... The VoiceAssistant-Eval dataset is not supposed to be used... for training models for cheating... require downstream users to implement consent gating and watermarking or traceability of synthetic audio.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: Code and data will be released at this page... The VoiceAssistant-Eval data and our open-source code are under an MIT license... We will maintain a data governance process for auditing and removal and reserve the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: "(4) Sampling: We sample data from the categorized problems to balance the ratio of different tasks."

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: "We preprocess the texts to ensure high synthesis quality: 1. Image references: We replace special tokens (e.g., '<image1>') with descriptive phrases... 2. Text rewriting: We use Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct ... to rewrite the text so it is more suitable for TTS... 3. Multiple-Choice Questions: We rephrase the options for better readability."; "(1) Deduplication: We use lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance to flag potential duplicate questions. Suspected duplicates are manually reviewed and removed"; "(2) Validation: We exclude incomplete or unsuitable instances, including entries with corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, and demonstrably incorrect answers."
